description:
Artifact for the paper Rule-Identity Shortcuts and Benign-Corpus Confounds in SIEM Alert-Triage Evaluation, submitted to Computers & Security (no DOI yet; it will be added on publication).

A majority-label-per-rule-identifier lookup table matches a trained two-layer Wazuh alert-triage pipeline (XGBoost for known attacks, a one-class SVM for novel ones) on the AIT-ADS benchmark. The effect is detector-specific, and on the authors' own Linux and Windows testbed collections several apparently strong results turn out to be artifacts of capture tempo, benign-corpus composition or small samples. The repository contains the five evaluation controls (C1-C5), the scripts that reproduce every figure and table of the paper (reproduce.sh), and the testbed collection.

Licences. Code and documentation: MIT (LICENSE). Data produced by the authors (testbed collection, result tables): CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA). Files derived from the AIT Alert Data Set (Landauer, Skopik and Wurzenberger, 10.5281/zenodo.8263181, CC BY 4.0) remain CC BY 4.0 and require attribution to its authors. The raw AIT-ADS files are not included; data/download_ait_ads.py downloads and verifies them.
